strategies.name: H13 relative momentum in QQQ (sleeve A)
strategies.rule: rs = NQ 09:00 ET hourly bar return minus the ES return of the same bar. Trade only when |rs| >= the rolling 60-session median of |rs| (30-session warm-up). Long QQQ if rs > 0, short if rs < 0, market order at 10:00. Stop
strategies.gate: just under EV and PF on the ETF execution; passed on NQ
strategies.sizing: $500 risk a trade: shares = 500 / (0.5 x ATR14)

strategies.name: Overnight QQQ + GLD book (sleeve B)
strategies.rule: Buy QQQ and GLD at 15:59 ET, 40% of equity each; sell both at 09:30:30 ET. No signal, no stop; 10% equity stop on the sleeve.
strategies.gate: passes all but the 1.5x drawdown line (rescaled to 3x in #35)

strategies.name: Trend filter, 10-month SMA (Faber GTAA)
strategies.rule: On the last trading day of each month: hold the asset if its close is above the 10-month simple moving average of month-end closes, else cash at the T-bill yield. GTAA-5 holds 20% in each of the five assets. Single-asset
strategies.verdict: risk reducer, not an edge; candidate overlay for a drawdown budget
strategies.selection: GTAA-5 2006-11 to 2025-10: Sharpe 0.66, +5.3% a year, MDD 15.2% (buy-and-hold 0.46, +6.8%, 45.8%); SPY single: Sharpe 0.82, MDD 24% vs 0.63, 55%

strategies.provenance: Faber (2007, updated 2013) A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation; Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen (2012) time-series momentum

strategies.name: Dual momentum (GEM)
strategies.rule: On the last trading day of each month compute 12-month returns. If SPY's 12-month return beats the T-bill 12-month return: hold SPY if it beats EFA over 12 months, else EFA. Otherwise hold AGG. 100% in one asset.
strategies.verdict: same Sharpe as SPY with less return
strategies.provenance: Antonacci (2014) Dual Momentum Investing; Jegadeesh and Titman (1993) momentum

strategies.name: Sector momentum, top 3 of 9 SPDRs
strategies.rule: On the last trading day of each month rank the nine sectors by the 6-month return ending one month earlier (skip the last month). Hold the top three, one third each. Trend filter: all cash when SPY's month-end close is b

log.text: The desks and the $50k plan. Mandate 4 widened the range: commodities, FX, rates, crypto and volatility desks each got pre-registered tests on execution-grade data (ETFs and spot; futures fronts as reads only). None passed alone: commodity trend on six ETFs is the one near miss (Sharpe 0.87, holdout 1.7), FX and rates trend are dead at our costs, bonds and commodities cannot cover a round trip in either session, crypto trend only trims buy-and-hold's drawdown and failed the last twelve months, short-vol carry keeps a one-day -26%, long-short sectors is noise. The allocation desk then sized the book: B 0.5x, C 0.75x, D 1.0x (commodity trend as a diversifier) with A at $500 risk a trade gives 11.1% a year at a 13.2% worst drawdown over 2005 to 2025, against 8.0% and 15.9% for the current book; overnight gross stays under 2x. The plan runs on paper from the next session; sleeve D rebalances monthly. The week before: the PC missed two exit sessions and ran the pre-ledger code; the overnight bot now adopts orphan lots.

Batches 1c and 2. Stocks: the RSI(2) rule generalises across 15 mega-caps (pooled +63 bps a trade on 3,877 trades, every name positive, holdout +128 bps on 131); overnight premiums are strongest in GOOGL and AVGO but any list of today's winners is hindsight, so no stock leg joins sleeve B. Minute bars 2016 to 2026: the pre-FOMC drift is real over 30 years (+13.7 bps into the statement night vs +3.7) and reversed in the last eight meetings; sleeve B already holds those nights. First-half-hour momentum entered at 15:30 and the last-30-minutes rule both lose net of costs in SPY and QQQ: retired. Gaps: QQQ gap-downs beyond 1 ATR bounce +47 bps by 10:29 (t 3.8) but only five times a year. Events calendar built from primary sources (263 FOMC days since 1994, CPI, NFP, PCE); every closed bot trade now gets an event-and-news attribution row.

Batch 1 results. One pass out of eleven pre-registered tests: Connors RSI(2) pullback in an uptrend (RSI(2) < 10 above the 200-day, exit above the 5-day). SPY +66 bps a trade on 253 trades since 1993 (CI +47 to +84, PF 3.12, t 6.8, walk-forward 3/3), QQQ +60 bps on 201 since 2000 (PF 2.23); holdout 12 and 11 trades at +90 and +77 bps; neighbours pass. It is sleeve C on paper from the next session (25% of equity per ETF, 15:57 ET run). Everything else failed its gate as written: trend filters halve drawdown but stay under Sharpe 1 (GTAA-5 0.66, SPY SMA 0.82 vs 0.63), dual momentum equals SPY, sector momentum 0.68 to 0.74 (fails Sharpe only), turn of the month is mostly the market's drift (excess t 1.0), the VIX overlay is rejected because stress nights pay more (+6.0 bps in backwardation), no ETF joins the overnight book (GDX passes alone but adds drawdown; bonds and commodities lose overnight), no weekday or pre-holiday filter, vol scaling +0.09 Sharpe (under the +0.10 line). Ledger: docs/strategy_ledger.md. Register: strategies/registry.json.

Mandate 3 pre-registration. A deterministic multi-strategy system across stocks and ETFs: every strategy fully specified in a register before any test; 49 daily histories pulled (SPY 1993, sectors 1998, GLD 2004, S&P index 1927); gates rescaled (log drawdown 3x annual); batch 1 = Faber 10-month SMA, dual momentum, sector momentum, RSI(2), turn of the month, VIX overlay, 29-ETF overnight scan, weekday read; batch 1b = vol-managed sizing, pre-holiday read; batch 2 (Alpaca minute data) = pre-FOMC drift, first-half-hour and last-30-minutes momentum, opening gap. Per-sleeve lot ledger so the bots share one account; event and news attribution on every closed trade (research/attribute_trades.py).

Report and Pine script. The Sleeves A and B backtest report (a Claude Doc) carries the rule, windows, statistics and charts for both sleeves: cumulative R for sleeve A, growth of $1 overnight vs intraday vs buy-and-hold and the yearly book bars for sleeve B. pine/baller_sleeves_qqq.pine draws every sleeve A trigger and the overnight P&L on a QQQ 15m chart (chart-window stats only; the backtest is the report). Billboard fixed on the desk; live file pushed from both machines. No new numbers.

Five markets ranked. Overnight drift, net of today's costs: QQQ +5.0 bps a night (t 4.5 on 6,694 nights, Sharpe 0.88, holdout 1.23; the day session earns nothing; buy-and-hold Sharpe 0.48), GLD +3.7 (t 3.4, Sharpe 0.75), SPY +3.0 (t 4.1, Sharpe 0.71); the QQQ + GLD book Sharpe 1.07 across 21 years and 1.05 in the holdout. IBIT and ETHA overnight were strong in 2024 to 2025 and negative in the last 12 months: failed. Crypto weekly momentum in spot fails on fees (62 switches a year); the 28-day filter only matches buy-and-hold with a smaller drawdown. BTC's best hours (16:00 to 18:00 ET, +7.7 bps, t 3.7) are worth less than one Alpaca round trip. Verdict: H13 in QQQ is the only per-trade edge; the overnight premium is the robust carry; nothing in ETH, nothing extra in SPY. Decision: paper book = sleeve A plus the overnight QQQ + GLD sleeve; overnight bot and schedules written and dry-run.

Where the return accrues. Two years of hourly bars: in every market we can trade on Alpaca the return comes while US cash equities are closed. QQQ overnight +4.4 bps a day against +1.7 intraday since 2004; GLD +4.4 against +0.2; gold futures +5.0 against -0.3; IBIT +18 against -6; BTC's strongest hours are 16:00 to 18:00 ET and 04:00 ET, US hours flat to negative. NQ's first-hour signal does not lead BTC (corr 0.05). Pre-registered: F1 overnight drift in the ETFs with a second gate set for daily-horizon rules, F3 crypto weekly momentum in spot, and three reads.

Mandate 2. Trade live, no prop firms: BTC, ETH, gold, QQQ, SPY; find what has edge, compare, pick the best. Costs pinned first: Alpaca crypto spot 0.25% taker a side, long only (0.55% a round trip at the market), so intraday crypto on spot is ruled out before any test; ETFs at $0.02 a share. Data pulled for all five markets, two years hourly and full daily history. Hypotheses drawn from the literature on crypto momentum, crypto time-of-day, gold fixes and the equity overnight drift.

ETF replication results. Building H13 from the ETFs themselves fails (+0.00R, PF 1.01): shift the window half an hour into the session and the signal is gone. The futures signal executed in QQQ carries over: selection N 212, +0.09R, PF 1.29, WF 3/3, one hundredth under the EV and PF gates; holdout N 56, +0.19R, PF 1.83; the 10:00 entry on 60 days of 15m bars reads +0.15R on 27. The last-half-hour momentum of Gao et al. is dead on QQQ and SPY 2023 to 2026 (-0.02R, PF 0.90, retired). The overnight drift is real (QQQ +5 bps a night since 1999, t 3.1; intraday -0.1 bps) but +0.06R a night, so an overlay question, not a standalone. Decisions: Track A in QQQ is the Alpaca paper rule; bot, read-only check and schedules written and dry-run; ETF costs $0.02 a share added to the protocol.

Batch 4 and H21 results. The Windows folder was uploaded back and every harness re-run here with the bundled environment: batch 2, H13 diagnostics and overlays, batch 3, the account and sizing studies, the gold flat-by test, H2 and H3. The Pine script shows the contract count in the trade label. Account spec plus sizing policy are the full plan for the Select 50K evaluation; nothing changes until Track E has 30 trades.

Sizing optimization and tweak tests. Six sizing policies and three tweaks, pre-registered, in-sample. Signal strength does not grade outcomes (weak tercile +0.39R, mid +0.06R, strong +0.27R), so strength-based sizing is dropped. The half-off level stays at +1R. The stop curve is bumpy (0.25 / 0.30 / 0.375 / 0.5 ATR: +0.21 / +0.21 / +0.24 / +0.18R), so the 0.375 point is partly luck and the honest claim is that the whole 0.25 to 0.5 band is positive. Sizing: the evaluation is drawdown-bound, and every added micro buys speed with failure risk at about 2 to 3 points of fail per 10 sessions saved. Fixed 1 MNQ 60% pass / 4% fail / median 79 sessions; $500 constant-dollar risk (a second micro only when the stop is 125 points or less) 69% / 10% / 68; 25% of buffer 65% / 5% / 69; fixed 2 MNQ 75% / 23% / 39. Pre-registered pick: $500 constant-dollar risk. No strategy tweak adopted; further tuning on 165 trades would fit noise.

Sized for Tradeify Select 50K. Rules as researched (verify on the dashboard): $3,000 target, $2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown that locks at $50,100 once the peak reaches $52,100, no daily loss limit, 40% consistency, 3 minimum days, 40 micros max, flat by 4:45 PM ET. The research spec's 0.5 ATR stop is $390 per MNQ and its historical drawdown $4,236 per micro: a poor fit (2 MNQ: 50% pass, 50% fail). Nine pre-registered variants, all in-sample: conviction days only with a 0.375 ATR stop and half off at +1R keeps EV at +0.24R, drops the historical drawdown to $1,780 per micro and the best day to $634, and bootstraps to 60% pass / 4% fail at 1 MNQ (median 79 sessions), 70% / 9% staged to 2 MNQ at $51k, 75% / 24% at 2 MNQ flat. The selection rule picks 1 MNQ. Gold forced flat at 16:00 loses its edge (PF 1.05) and is out for this account. Track D gold on the forward log; H13 Pine script (pine/cues_h13_nq.pine) drawing entry, red stop box and green exit box per trade with width equal to duration; Tradeify rules researched and account variants pre-registered.

Batch 3: H13 as a driving factor. Can H13 days be entered better? No. A pullback entry with a structure stop lost -0.25R with 79% stopped; the 0.5 ATR stop at 10:00 is the mechanism, since NQ's hourly noise exceeds any pullback bar. Do the days H13 skips have an edge? No: fading the first hour +0.02R, following it +0.04R, both noise. Does a European-open window stack? No: 217 trades, EV -0.01R, and uncorrelated with H13 (-0.03). Management: taking half off at +1R keeps EV at +0.12R while cutting the top-10 share from 84% to 62% and drawdown from 9.7R to 8.8R; no EV lift, so no new track, but the forward log now records each trade's best and worst excursion so this can be read off the forward data later. Conclusion: H13 is one-dimensional and already used as well as this data allows. What adds on is a different instrument.

Batch 3 pre-registered. Nanon asked to use H13 as a driving factor and look for add-ons. Three questions, one family each: H14 better entries on H13 days, H16 the quiet days H13 skips, H15 European-open momentum as a second window; plus H17, three management rules on the H13 base, judged in-sample only.

Overlay study, second track earned. On the 209 H13 base trades (selection only, the holdout is spent): daily-trend agreement hurts (EV +0.07R) and its counter-trend control helps (+0.17R), which reads as noise; volume participation hurts (+0.08R); first-hour conviction (the 09:00 bar closes in the outer third of its range in the signal direction) lifts EV to +0.18R, PF 1.73, WF 3/3 and cuts the top-10 share from 84% to 64% on N=165; the higher-volatility half carries the edge (+0.18R above the ATR median, -0.04R below), in line with the paper. Conviction meets the pre-registered rule and becomes Track B. Both overlays run at 1.7 to 1.8 trades a week on selection, under the 2 a week floor. Nothing is combined. These are in-sample numbers and the least trustworthy in this log; only the forward tracks can confirm them.

H7 parked, H1 added to the forward log. Free 5m bars cover 118 sessions in two windows, about 22 of them inside the H13 selection window; a lower-timeframe delta filter cannot be validated on that. The H1 15m rule, frozen since entry #2, joins the daily forward log as Track C. H13 diagnostics, forward test started. Neighbors: every one keeps a positive EV (stop 0.375 to 0.625 ATR, window 45 to 75, filter 1.25x). So it is first-hour momentum held to the close, sharpened a little by ES. Cuts: shorts +0.16R, longs +0.08R; 2025H2 was negative; the top 10 of 209 trades carry 84% of the profit, without them EV is +0.02R. Verdict: passes the gates, fragile. Batch 2 results. 22 variants across five families on 451 selection sessions of 1H bars, 135 holdout. H4 gap fade: primary EV -0.03R, holdout -0.29R; retired. H13 ES relative strength: unfiltered +0.09R on selection, -0.02R on holdout; the magnitude-filtered variant N=209, EV +0.12R, CI above zero, PF 1.42, WF 3/3, 2.3 a week, then holdout N=47, EV +0.08R, PF 1.30. Free data only. Nanon declined the data purchase. Checked what Yahoo's daily bars are: the open is the 18:00 ET Globex open and the close is the 17:00 settlement, so they cannot carry regular-hours day-trade rules. Pre-registered five families on 1H: H4 gap fade, H8 first-hour breakout, H9 midday continuation, H10 1H mean reversion, H13 ES relative strength.

H3 overnight hold tested. 477 selection sessions on 2y of 1H bars, 134 holdout. The pre-registered primary (long after a down day, stop 0.5 daily ATR, exit at 09:00): EV +0.045R, CI [-0.06, +0.16], PF 1.15, WF 2/3. Fails. The control (after an up day) did better: EV +0.09R, PF 1.42. The conditioning idea is wrong. Long every night: N=477, EV +0.072R, CI [+0.005, +0.137], PF 1.28, WF 3/3, 5 a week, +11 pts a night, holdout EV +0.09R and PF 1.31. The CI clears zero on both windows, but it misses the +0.10R and PF 1.30 gates, the sample is a two-year bull run, and the hold runs 17 hours, which prop-firm rules do not allow. Parked as a measured fact. Standing: 0 of 3 candidates pass. H4 next.

H2 5-min ORB tested. Pre-registered the paper's rule (first 5-min candle sets direction, enter 09:35, stop at the other side of the candle floored at 0.10 daily ATR, target 10R or 15:55 close, 0.70 pt costs). Selection: 48 sessions Mar 2 to May 7. Primary: WR 21%, EV -0.34R, PF 0.58, -16.2R, WF 1/3, 38 of 48 stopped, the 10R target never hit. Every secondary negative too: 2R, 3R, EOD exit, stop 0.75x and 1.25x, gap-agreement filter, 1 pt slippage stress. Holdout (48 sessions Aug 6 to Oct 13, one look): primary EV +0.08R, PF 1.12. A rule that fails selection is not rescued by its holdout. Pooled 96 sessions: EV -0.13R, PF 0.82, 1 target hit. H2 retired on free data.

Paused on the Mac, moved to the Windows PC. The Mac session handed off via the firm/windows bundle (research kit, data, docs). On Windows: Python 3.13 environment built (the 3.15 numpy DLLs were blocked by Smart App Control until Nanon turned it off). The H1 harness rerun on Windows reproduces entry #2 to the third decimal. H2 pre-registered in the log before its harness was written.

H6 break-even study. PDHL fade (N=222) and ORB (N=186) replayed under ten stop rules on the selection window. PDHL: 49% of trades reach +1R, then 44% go to target and 49% come back to the stop; 36% of eventual winners touch entry again after +1R. Every profit-threshold break-even rule loses versus no rule (BE at +1R: -25R; BE at +0.5R: -26R; stop-to-level: -13R to -20R). Only a time-based cut (BE after 8 bars if positive) helped, +8R, and the setup is still negative. ORB: stopped trades almost never saw +1R first (4%), 63% are time exits, every BE rule hurts. Rule going forward: a stop moves on time or structure, never on profit, and only on a setup with edge. Windows bundle built.

H3 measured, H1 tested. Drift on 2y of 1H bars accrues outside RTH: Asia +3.6 bps/day (t 1.7), Europe +2.6 (t 1.2), RTH +1.2 (t 0.3); the 03:00 ET hour (European open) is the strongest single hour. H1 at the 1-hour proxy shows nothing (t -1.2 on 451 sessions, every variant negative); retired. H1 at the paper's 30-minute granularity shows the effect: t 1.9, sign agreement 55%, primary rule EV +0.12R, PF 1.39, 3 of 3 walk-forward blocks, 5 trades a week, 22% stopped, +9.4 pts a trade after costs. N=157 and the CI spans zero, so no gate pass. The agreement filter gives 2.6 trades a week at EV +0.09R on N=80. To settle H1 we need 2 to 3 years of 15m bars: buy from Databento or forward-test for about five months. Decision is Nanon's. Next: H2 5-min ORB, H3 overnight-hold rule.
